description: Is the Software Factory healthy now, and what is each ticket doing? Live health, in-range KPIs, tickets in flight, change reviews, and failures that need action. Detail tables, charts and raw logs sit under collapsed Debug rows. Prometheus counts are approximate; log lines are the reference for ticket stages. The delivery story is on Factory business.

panels.description: How to read Factory ops.

options.content: **Now** is the last 15 minutes: stuck tickets, errors, ack speed. **In range** is the time window you picked — Cost with Service=All matches Factory business Spend. **Tickets** lists what is in flight (furthest stage and change review). Open a **Debug** row only when you need the underlying lines or charts.

panels.title: Overview

panels.description: Tickets waiting past a hop deadline now. Calm at 0, orange from 1, red from 3. Stuck means the hop-watch deadline passed with no outcome posted (factory-desk lib/hop-watch.ts): the ticket's latest announce is Triaged, older than 15 min (the planner has not answered), or Approved, older than 7 min (the worker has not launched). An outcome the desk announces while the status stays put (needs info, plan stopped, approved without plan, launch failed) is the newer state, so that ticket is not stuck. The hop watch posts in the ticket's thread at those deadlines; this is the same rule, read now. Planned has no deadline (it waits for a person) and To Do has no announce span, so neither is here. Reads the last 7 days of status changes, so a ticket stuck for longer is missed.

targets.query: { resource.service.namespace = "software-factory" && name = "factory.background" && span.factory.delivery.kind =~ "jira[.]announce[.](triaged|planned|approved|in_progress|in_review|done|needs_info|plan_stopped|approved_without_plan|launch_failed)" && span.factory.ticket.key != nil } | select(span.factory.ticket.key, span.factory.delivery.kind)

panels.title: Stuck now

panels.description: Deliveries whose factory.outcome is an error (error|http_5..|bad_args|failed|.*_failed|threw|.*_threw|config_error|launch_timeout|unauthorized|.*_unreadable|unavailable|claim_unavailable|gave_up) in the last 15 minutes. panels.title: Tool fails

panels.description: p95 of the factory.delivery span (the webhook or hook handler up to its reply) in the last 15 minutes. Target: under 3 s (orange), 10 s is red. Background work, reminders and cloud-agent launches are not in it (see Debug: latency). Quantiles interpolate inside histogram buckets, so at low volume p95 reads as the upper edge of the bucket it falls in ("≤ that edge"), not an exact value. Some of these histogram series have two writers (a restored VM rewriting its series), so the quantile is noisy, and no panel uses the _sum/_count mean, which those series make unreliable. These 15-minute stats use a 1m subquery step, not the dashboard ${prom_res}, so a 7d+ view still counts all 15 minutes. On a live range the newest scrape can sit after the last whole 1m step (≤ one scrape of lag versus Loki).

panels.title: Deliveries

panels.description: Tickets waiting past a hop deadline now, longest first: the stage they are in, since when, and for how long. Orange past the deadline, red after an hour. Stuck means the hop-watch deadline passed with no outcome posted (factory-desk lib/hop-watch.ts): the ticket's latest announce is Triaged, older than 15 min (the planner has not answered), or Approved, older than 7 min (the worker has not launched). An outcome the desk announces while the status stays put (needs info, plan stopped, approved without plan, launch failed) is the newer state, so that ticket is not stuck. The hop watch posts in the ticket's thread at those deadlines; this is the same rule, read now. Planned has no deadline (it waits for a person) and To Do has no announce span, so neither is here. Reads the last 7 days of status changes, so a ticket stuck for longer is missed.

defaults.noValue: No ticket is past a hop deadline. Nothing to do.

panels.description: p95 of the factory.delivery span in range. Target: under 3 s (orange), 10 s is red. Background work, reminders and cloud-agent launches are not in it (see Debug: latency). Quantiles interpolate inside histogram buckets, so at low volume p95 reads as the upper edge of the bucket it falls in ("≤ that edge"), not an exact value. Some of these histogram series have two writers (a restored VM rewriting its series), so the quantile is noisy, and no panel uses the _sum/_count mean, which those series make unreliable.

panels.title: Ack p95

panels.description: ESTIMATE, not billing: tokens × the price variables (USD per 1M tokens, Cursor list prices from https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing, retrieved 2026-10-03; default Grok 4.6 Fast: $4 input, $1 cache read, $12 output, reasoning $0 because it is inside output). Uncached input is priced at the input price and cache reads once at the cache price. Input has two shapes on this metric and no label tells them apart: a host turn (desk, triage, the planner before #227) reports it gross (cache reads inside it), a cloud turn (the planner since #227, the worker since #229) reports it net of cache reads. Uncached input is decided per series before any sum, as July's own turn-cost.js toCatalogDisjointUsage does: input - cache_read where cache_read <= input (gross), the whole input where cache_read > input (net) or where there is no cache_read series. A cloud series whose input happens to reach its cache reads is read as gross and undercounted by them; one series (one process life, one session, one ticket) that mixes local and cloud turns is classified as a whole. July 0.2.20 dropped cursor.cost.usage; 0.2.24 still emits no USD cost metric and no model label on turn.completed. Spend here is always tokens × the price variables, not an invoice and not July's old cost counter. So one price set is applied to every slug. Hosts on Cursor Auto bill at the list price of whatever model each request was routed to (Grok 4.6 $2/$0.5/$6, Claude Opus 5.5 $4/$0.20/$20); neither Auto routing nor the Cursor Token Rate for third-party models is modelled. Built from token counters, so it is approximate like them. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference. Set var-price_input (and the other price_* variables) in the URL or Settings → Variables. With Service=All this matches Factory business Spend. Narrow Service to one factory-* slug to see that host only. Breakdown under Debug: cost.

panels.title: Cost

panels.description: Share of the prompt input in range that was served from cache: cache_read / (uncached input + cache_read), with uncached input decided per series. Input has two shapes on this metric and no label tells them apart: a host turn (desk, triage, the planner before #227) reports it gross (cache reads inside it), a cloud turn (the planner since #227, the worker since #229) reports it net of cache reads. Uncached input is decided per series before any sum, as July's own turn-cost.js toCatalogDisjointUsage does: input - cache_read where cache_read <= input (gross), the whole input where cache_read > input (net) or where there is no cache_read series. A cloud series whose input happens to reach its cache reads is read as gross and undercounted by them; one series (one process life, one session, one ticket) that mixes local and cloud turns is classified as a whole.

panels.description: Distinct tickets with a plan start check in range whose result was retried, not_moved, final: the desk's 4-minute check found no sign of the planner running (retried = the ticket was re-sent once, final = it gave up after that one retry, not_moved = the re-send could not move the ticket). One per ticket, so a ticket that was retried and then given up on counts once. Calm at 0, red from 1. A healthy check logs started and is the neutral tile beside this one. Factory fields are read from structured metadata on older records, else parsed from the raw util.format body (a JSON line, or a [tag] line's key=value pairs). The console bridge exports lines as raw util.format bodies and does not parse them into attributes.

panels.description: The 20 tickets that most recently reached their furthest pipeline stage in the last 7 days (whatever the dashboard range), newest first: current stage, how long in it, and since when. Click a key to open Jira or filter this dashboard to its journey, or type one in Ticket. Empty while a ticket is selected. Current stage is the furthest milestone the ticket has reached in the last 7 days (filed → planned → approved → building → PR opened → merged), from the hosts' own JSON console lines — the same milestones as Factory business Ticket flow. Merged beats every earlier stage even when a newer log line names an earlier one. Tempo announce spans are lossy and are not used here. Merged here includes a Done PR whose Jira board was not moved (pr_status stage=done, outcome not_moved); Factory business Merged still requires moved. The desk's announce spans can be lost at flush (in the 2026-10-05 audit 7 of 25 status changes in 24h had no span), so span-based stage panels can miss a change; the Loki milestone panels (the Business flow and lead times, Ticket milestones on Factory ops) read the hosts' own JSON lines, one per milestone, and are the reference.

panels.description: Factory error and warning log lines per bucket, stacked by level (error red, warn orange; the Slack WebClient session-stopped pair left out). Each bar is the count of matching log lines in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Loki uses $__auto with step=$bucket and a one-step negative offset so the in-progress bucket is included (a 5m bucket over more than about 38 days exceeds Loki's 11,000-point limit). On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. On a range that ends before now, the last bar covers its whole bucket and can include up to one step after the range end. LogQL has no subqueries, so a Loki bar cannot be capped at $__to. The first bar starts at the first step boundary at or after the range start, so events between the range start and that boundary (up to one step) are in the range stats but in no bar, and the left edge can show a gap. Quote the range stats.

The console bridge exports lines as raw util.format bodies and does not parse them into attributes.

panels.title: Health event lines (plan start watch, worker decisions, review updates)

panels.description: One line per milestone from the hosts' own JSON console lines, newest first: plan started and plan turn completed / failed (planner), the plan start check (desk), approved (a Slack reaction or a typed approve; the approve tool and a board drag log no desk line, so the worker's decision is the sign of those), worker launched / turn sent / launch failed (with via and whether it was a retry), PR opened and PR in review, review updates with the change-review state, and merged. panels.title: Ticket journey: events in time order

panels.description: Factory deliveries per bucket, stacked by slug, hop-watch ticks included. All six factory slugs are always listed; an idle slug shows 0. Each bar is the count in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Prometheus uses $__interval, a one-step negative offset, and a ${prom_res} subquery (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) that keeps only samples with from ≤ time() ≤ to. The last bar on a range that ends before now stops at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (the subquery grid); a range end that is not on that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step of events out of both the bars and the range stats (the two still agree). The first bar can start one step before $__from while counting only samples at or after $__from. The step is $bucket; Prometheus widens it on long ranges. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. The range stats and tables are the totals for the whole window. They use the same ${prom_res} subquery and reset rule as the bars. For _total, the subquery inner is max_over_time(s[${smooth}]) (${smooth} is 2m below 7d, 5m at 7d+, always at least ${prom_res}). increase() runs when that smoothed window dropped (resets>0), including a restart whose new life passes the old maximum; on a range no longer than about ${smooth} plus one step, a single restart near the range start is also counted from the raw samples. Flips shorter than ${smooth} become a stable high-water mark. Flips longer than ${smooth} can make a bar take increase() leftover. Writer flips longer than ${smooth} are read as restarts; bars and range can then both read many times high — each flip re-counts up to the counter's full lifetime value — and Loki/Tempo are the reference. Otherwise, after a plain restart the range and the bars are both increase() estimates (±10–20%). Per-bucket Prometheus legends match the range within that leftover, rounding on count bars, and up to one ${prom_res} step when $__to is not on the subquery grid (bars and range stats then both omit it). A Loki bar chart can include the last bar past a range that ends before now and can miss up to one step at the range start. Quote the range stats; treat bars after a restart as estimates. Counted with counter_inc (see the folder README): hosted VMs are short-lived and each is its own series, which increase() and rate() would undercount. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference.

panels.title: Deliveries per bucket by outcome class

panels.description: July turn.completed and turn.failed records per bucket (failed leaves out expected customer-state errors, as the Turn fails tiles do). Each series is 0 in every bucket that had a turn, so a flat failed series means no failed turn, not a missing feed. Only factory-desk, factory-planner and factory-security-reviewer run model turns; the other slugs show 0. The In range Turns tile counts the Prometheus turn counter (approximate) instead, so the two can differ. Each bar is the count of matching log lines in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Loki uses $__auto with step=$bucket and a one-step negative offset so the in-progress bucket is included (a 5m bucket over more than about 38 days exceeds Loki's 11,000-point limit). On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. On a range that ends before now, the last bar covers its whole bucket and can include up to one step after the range end. LogQL has no subqueries, so a Loki bar cannot be capped at $__to. The first bar starts at the first step boundary at or after the range start, so events between the range start and that boundary (up to one step) are in the range stats but in no bar, and the left edge can show a gap. Quote the range stats.

panels.title: Failures and warnings

panels.description: Estimated spend in the time range by factory service. ESTIMATE, not billing: tokens × the price variables (USD per 1M tokens, Cursor list prices from https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing, retrieved 2026-10-03; default Grok 4.6 Fast: $4 input, $1 cache read, $12 output, reasoning $0 because it is inside output). Uncached input is priced at the input price and cache reads once at the cache price. Input has two shapes on this metric and no label tells them apart: a host turn (desk, triage, the planner before #227) reports it gross (cache reads inside it), a cloud turn (the planner since #227, the worker since #229) reports it net of cache reads. Uncached input is decided per series before any sum, as July's own turn-cost.js toCatalogDisjointUsage does: input - cache_read where cache_read <= input (gross), the whole input where cache_read > input (net) or where there is no cache_read series. A cloud series whose input happens to reach its cache reads is read as gross and undercounted by them; one series (one process life, one session, one ticket) that mixes local and cloud turns is classified as a whole. July 0.2.20 dropped cursor.cost.usage; 0.2.24 still emits no USD cost metric and no model label on turn.completed. Spend here is always tokens × the price variables, not an invoice and not July's old cost counter. So one price set is applied to every slug. Hosts on Cursor Auto bill at the list price of whatever model each request was routed to (Grok 4.6 $2/$0.5/$6, Claude Opus 5.5 $4/$0.20/$20); neither Auto routing nor the Cursor Token Rate for third-party models is modelled. Built from token counters, so it is approximate like them. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference. Set var-price_input (and the other price_* variables) in the URL or Settings → Variables.

panels.title: Spend by service

panels.description: All six factory slugs are always listed; an idle slug shows 0. Only factory-desk, factory-planner and factory-security-reviewer run model turns; the other slugs show 0. ESTIMATE, not billing: tokens × the price variables (USD per 1M tokens, Cursor list prices from https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing, retrieved 2026-10-03; default Grok 4.6 Fast: $4 input, $1 cache read, $12 output, reasoning $0 because it is inside output). Uncached input is priced at the input price and cache reads once at the cache price. Input has two shapes on this metric and no label tells them apart: a host turn (desk, triage, the planner before #227) reports it gross (cache reads inside it), a cloud turn (the planner since #227, the worker since #229) reports it net of cache reads. Uncached input is decided per series before any sum, as July's own turn-cost.js toCatalogDisjointUsage does: input - cache_read where cache_read <= input (gross), the whole input where cache_read > input (net) or where there is no cache_read series. A cloud series whose input happens to reach its cache reads is read as gross and undercounted by them; one series (one process life, one session, one ticket) that mixes local and cloud turns is classified as a whole. July 0.2.20 dropped cursor.cost.usage; 0.2.24 still emits no USD cost metric and no model label on turn.completed. Spend here is always tokens × the price variables, not an invoice and not July's old cost counter. So one price set is applied to every slug. Hosts on Cursor Auto bill at the list price of whatever model each request was routed to (Grok 4.6 $2/$0.5/$6, Claude Opus 5.5 $4/$0.20/$20); neither Auto routing nor the Cursor Token Rate for third-party models is modelled. Built from token counters, so it is approximate like them. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference. Set var-price_input (and the other price_* variables) in the URL or Settings → Variables. Each bar is the count in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Prometheus uses $__interval, a one-step negative offset, and a ${prom_res} subquery (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) that keeps only samples with from ≤ time() ≤ to. The last bar on a range that ends before now stops at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (the subquery grid); a range end that is not on that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step of events out of both the bars and the range stats (the two still agree). The first bar can start one step before $__from while counting only samples at or after $__from. The step is $bucket; Prometheus widens it on long ranges. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. The range stats and tables are the totals for the whole window. They use the same ${prom_res} subquery and reset rule as the bars. For _total, the subquery inner is max_over_time(s[${smooth}]) (${smooth} is 2m below 7d, 5m at 7d+, always at least ${prom_res}). increase() runs when that smoothed window dropped (resets>0), including a restart whose new life passes the old maximum; on a range no longer than about ${smooth} plus one step, a single restart near the range start is also counted from the raw samples. Flips shorter than ${smooth} become a stable high-water mark. Flips longer than ${smooth} can make a bar take increase() leftover. Writer flips longer than ${smooth} are read as restarts; bars and range can then both read many times high — each flip re-counts up to the counter's full lifetime value — and Loki/Tempo are the reference. Otherwise, after a plain restart the range and the bars are both increase() estimates (±10–20%). Per-bucket Prometheus legends match the range within that leftover, rounding on count bars, and up to one ${prom_res} step when $__to is not on the subquery grid (bars and range stats then both omit it). A Loki bar chart can include the last bar past a range that ends before now and can miss up to one step at the range start. Quote the range stats; treat bars after a restart as estimates. Counted with counter_inc (see the folder README): hosted VMs are short-lived and each is its own series, which increase() and rate() would undercount. panels.title: Cost / bucket

panels.description: Mean full cost of the tickets merged in the trailing 24h: for each ticket merged in that window, its own end-to-end estimated cost from factory_ticket_key over the last 7 days (summed over every host that tagged the key; the Service filter does not apply), then the mean across those merged tickets. Unkeyed turns (factory_ticket_key none or other) and tickets not merged in the window contribute nothing. The points are the same mean per 6h bucket. Tickets merged before the ticket key was deployed (2026-10-04 04:43 UTC) carry no key, so the line starts from then; it has a value only once a merged ticket's key also appears on the token and cost counters. Excludes the worker's cloud build agent (launched through @cursor/sdk, not counted by July); the planner's cloud turns (since #227) and the worker's July cloud turn (since #229) are counted, and report input net of cache reads, which the per-series uncached rule prices in full. Counter-based figures can read high after a host changes its service instance id if the restore carried nonzero totals: the new series starts at them, and they are counted again. The factory draws one id per process life and does not rebase; nothing records a value before the first request, so a new life normally starts at its own increments. Two lives that share an id are not repaired, and a pod frozen before its next 10 s export loses that interval. Loki and Tempo are the reference. ESTIMATE, not billing: tokens × the price variables (USD per 1M tokens, Cursor list prices from https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing, retrieved 2026-10-03; default Grok 4.6 Fast: $4 input, $1 cache read, $12 output, reasoning $0 because it is inside output). Uncached input is priced at the input price and cache reads once at the cache price. panels.title: Cost by ticket

panels.description: How the cost estimate is made, and what it leaves out.

options.content:
July 0.2.20 dropped `cursor.cost.usage`; 0.2.24 still emits no USD cost metric and no `cursor.model.name` / `agent_sdk.cost_usd` on new turns. Cost here is tokens × the hidden price variables (USD per 1M tokens, [Cursor list prices](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing), retrieved 2026-10-03), by design, not a workaround for a late estimate. Defaults are Grok 4.6 Fast, the desk's and triage's model: $4 input, $1 cache read, $12 output; reasoning $0 because reasoning tokens are counted inside output. Uncached input is priced at the input price and cache reads once at the cache price. Historical `cursor_cost_usage_USD_total` series, if still in the store, are unused.

The planner, worker, fixer and reviewer run Cursor Auto, which bills at the list price of whatever model each request is routed to. Auto routing and the Cursor Token Rate for third-party models are not modelled.

**Engineer-hours saved** is a model, not a measurement: merged tickets × the Hours / ticket variable (default 4 h). Change the variable to change the model.

panels.title: Estimate, not billing

panels.description: One row per slug. Input (gross) is input as reported: gross on a host turn, net of cache reads on a cloud turn; Uncached is decided per series (input - cache_read on a gross series, the whole input on a net one). All six factory slugs are always listed; an idle slug shows 0. Only factory-desk, factory-planner and factory-security-reviewer run model turns; the other slugs show 0. ESTIMATE, not billing: tokens × the price variables (USD per 1M tokens, Cursor list prices from https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing, retrieved 2026-10-03; default Grok 4.6 Fast: $4 input, $1 cache read, $12 output, reasoning $0 because it is inside output). Uncached input is priced at the input price and cache reads once at the cache price. Input has two shapes on this metric and no label tells them apart: a host turn (desk, triage, the planner before #227) reports it gross (cache reads inside it), a cloud turn (the planner since #227, the worker since #229) reports it net of cache reads. Uncached input is decided per series before any sum, as July's own turn-cost.js toCatalogDisjointUsage does: input - cache_read where cache_read <= input (gross), the whole input where cache_read > input (net) or where there is no cache_read series. A cloud series whose input happens to reach its cache reads is read as gross and undercounted by them; one series (one process life, one session, one ticket) that mixes local and cloud turns is classified as a whole. July 0.2.20 dropped cursor.cost.usage; 0.2.24 still emits no USD cost metric and no model label on turn.completed. Spend here is always tokens × the price variables, not an invoice and not July's old cost counter. So one price set is applied to every slug. Hosts on Cursor Auto bill at the list price of whatever model each request was routed to (Grok 4.6 $2/$0.5/$6, Claude Opus 5.5 $4/$0.20/$20); neither Auto routing nor the Cursor Token Rate for third-party models is modelled. Built from token counters, so it is approximate like them. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference. Set var-price_input (and the other price_* variables) in the URL or Settings → Variables.

panels.title: Tokens and cost by service

panels.description: Counts in the time range. Span is almost always factory.delivery; Kind already tells the story. Click a service to open its logs. Counted with counter_inc (see the folder README): hosted VMs are short-lived and each is its own series, which increase() and rate() would undercount. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference. Counter-based figures can read high after a host changes its service instance id if the restore carried nonzero totals: the new series starts at them, and they are counted again. The factory draws one id per process life and does not rebase; nothing records a value before the first request, so a new life normally starts at its own increments. Two lives that share an id are not repaired, and a pod frozen before its next 10 s export loses that interval. Loki and Tempo are the reference.

panels.description: Outcomes that are errors (error|http_5..|bad_args|failed|.*_failed|threw|.*_threw|config_error|launch_timeout|unauthorized|.*_unreadable|unavailable|claim_unavailable|gave_up) or no-ops (http_4..|ignored|ignored_comment|duplicate|deduped|skipped|skip|stop|action_skipped|none|idle|not_launched|not_started|not_posted|not_armed|not_moved|not_watched|refused|staging_refused|superseded|in_flight|no_run|no_brief|no_branch), from the factory code's vocabulary. Empty is good. Counter-based figures can read high after a host changes its service instance id if the restore carried nonzero totals: the new series starts at them, and they are counted again. The factory draws one id per process life and does not rebase; nothing records a value before the first request, so a new life normally starts at its own increments. Two lives that share an id are not repaired, and a pod frozen before its next 10 s export loses that interval. Loki and Tempo are the reference.

panels.description: Agent turns per bucket by agent_sdk.turn_status (completed, failed, or an expected-error class). Each bar is the count in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Prometheus uses $__interval, a one-step negative offset, and a ${prom_res} subquery (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) that keeps only samples with from ≤ time() ≤ to. The last bar on a range that ends before now stops at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (the subquery grid); a range end that is not on that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step of events out of both the bars and the range stats (the two still agree). The first bar can start one step before $__from while counting only samples at or after $__from. The step is $bucket; Prometheus widens it on long ranges. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. The range stats and tables are the totals for the whole window. They use the same ${prom_res} subquery and reset rule as the bars. For _total, the subquery inner is max_over_time(s[${smooth}]) (${smooth} is 2m below 7d, 5m at 7d+, always at least ${prom_res}). increase() runs when that smoothed window dropped (resets>0), including a restart whose new life passes the old maximum; on a range no longer than about ${smooth} plus one step, a single restart near the range start is also counted from the raw samples. Flips shorter than ${smooth} become a stable high-water mark. Flips longer than ${smooth} can make a bar take increase() leftover. Writer flips longer than ${smooth} are read as restarts; bars and range can then both read many times high — each flip re-counts up to the counter's full lifetime value — and Loki/Tempo are the reference. Otherwise, after a plain restart the range and the bars are both increase() estimates (±10–20%). Per-bucket Prometheus legends match the range within that leftover, rounding on count bars, and up to one ${prom_res} step when $__to is not on the subquery grid (bars and range stats then both omit it). A Loki bar chart can include the last bar past a range that ends before now and can miss up to one step at the range start. Quote the range stats; treat bars after a restart as estimates. Counted with counter_inc (see the folder README): hosted VMs are short-lived and each is its own series, which increase() and rate() would undercount. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference.

panels.title: Sessions per bucket by channel

panels.description: agent_sdk_hosted_execution_visible_reply_total counts each hosted execution once. Its outcome (visible reply, error, none), channel_kind and delivery_surface labels are kept; this panel counts executions per slug, not replies. All six factory slugs are always listed; an idle slug shows 0. Each bar is the count in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Prometheus uses $__interval, a one-step negative offset, and a ${prom_res} subquery (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) that keeps only samples with from ≤ time() ≤ to. The last bar on a range that ends before now stops at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (the subquery grid); a range end that is not on that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step of events out of both the bars and the range stats (the two still agree). The first bar can start one step before $__from while counting only samples at or after $__from. The step is $bucket; Prometheus widens it on long ranges. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. The range stats and tables are the totals for the whole window. They use the same ${prom_res} subquery and reset rule as the bars. For _total, the subquery inner is max_over_time(s[${smooth}]) (${smooth} is 2m below 7d, 5m at 7d+, always at least ${prom_res}). increase() runs when that smoothed window dropped (resets>0), including a restart whose new life passes the old maximum; on a range no longer than about ${smooth} plus one step, a single restart near the range start is also counted from the raw samples. Flips shorter than ${smooth} become a stable high-water mark. Flips longer than ${smooth} can make a bar take increase() leftover. Writer flips longer than ${smooth} are read as restarts; bars and range can then both read many times high — each flip re-counts up to the counter's full lifetime value — and Loki/Tempo are the reference. Otherwise, after a plain restart the range and the bars are both increase() estimates (±10–20%). Per-bucket Prometheus legends match the range within that leftover, rounding on count bars, and up to one ${prom_res} step when $__to is not on the subquery grid (bars and range stats then both omit it). A Loki bar chart can include the last bar past a range that ends before now and can miss up to one step at the range start. Quote the range stats; treat bars after a restart as estimates. Counted with counter_inc (see the folder README): hosted VMs are short-lived and each is its own series, which increase() and rate() would undercount. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference.

panels.description: July hosted HTTP requests per bucket, platform routes (.*/(health|healthz|ready|readyz|live|livez|guest-network|manifest)) left out. Colour is the slug, then 4xx/5xx. Each bar is the count in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Prometheus uses $__interval, a one-step negative offset, and a ${prom_res} subquery (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) that keeps only samples with from ≤ time() ≤ to. The last bar on a range that ends before now stops at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (the subquery grid); a range end that is not on that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step of events out of both the bars and the range stats (the two still agree). The first bar can start one step before $__from while counting only samples at or after $__from. The step is $bucket; Prometheus widens it on long ranges. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. The range stats and tables are the totals for the whole window. They use the same ${prom_res} subquery and reset rule as the bars. For _total, the subquery inner is max_over_time(s[${smooth}]) (${smooth} is 2m below 7d, 5m at 7d+, always at least ${prom_res}). increase() runs when that smoothed window dropped (resets>0), including a restart whose new life passes the old maximum; on a range no longer than about ${smooth} plus one step, a single restart near the range start is also counted from the raw samples. Flips shorter than ${smooth} become a stable high-water mark. Flips longer than ${smooth} can make a bar take increase() leftover. Writer flips longer than ${smooth} are read as restarts; bars and range can then both read many times high — each flip re-counts up to the counter's full lifetime value — and Loki/Tempo are the reference. Otherwise, after a plain restart the range and the bars are both increase() estimates (±10–20%). Per-bucket Prometheus legends match the range within that leftover, rounding on count bars, and up to one ${prom_res} step when $__to is not on the subquery grid (bars and range stats then both omit it). A Loki bar chart can include the last bar past a range that ends before now and can miss up to one step at the range start. Quote the range stats; treat bars after a restart as estimates. Counted with counter_inc (see the folder README): hosted VMs are short-lived and each is its own series, which increase() and rate() would undercount. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference.

panels.title: Tokens per bucket: uncached input, cache read, output

panels.description: Input + output per bucket, stacked by slug (input as reported: gross on a host turn, net of cache reads on a cloud turn). All six factory slugs are always listed; an idle slug shows 0. Only factory-desk, factory-planner and factory-security-reviewer run model turns; the other slugs show 0. Each bar is the count in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Prometheus uses $__interval, a one-step negative offset, and a ${prom_res} subquery (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) that keeps only samples with from ≤ time() ≤ to. The last bar on a range that ends before now stops at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (the subquery grid); a range end that is not on that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step of events out of both the bars and the range stats (the two still agree). The first bar can start one step before $__from while counting only samples at or after $__from. The step is $bucket; Prometheus widens it on long ranges. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. The range stats and tables are the totals for the whole window. They use the same ${prom_res} subquery and reset rule as the bars. For _total, the subquery inner is max_over_time(s[${smooth}]) (${smooth} is 2m below 7d, 5m at 7d+, always at least ${prom_res}). increase() runs when that smoothed window dropped (resets>0), including a restart whose new life passes the old maximum; on a range no longer than about ${smooth} plus one step, a single restart near the range start is also counted from the raw samples. Flips shorter than ${smooth} become a stable high-water mark. Flips longer than ${smooth} can make a bar take increase() leftover. Writer flips longer than ${smooth} are read as restarts; bars and range can then both read many times high — each flip re-counts up to the counter's full lifetime value — and Loki/Tempo are the reference. Otherwise, after a plain restart the range and the bars are both increase() estimates (±10–20%). Per-bucket Prometheus legends match the range within that leftover, rounding on count bars, and up to one ${prom_res} step when $__to is not on the subquery grid (bars and range stats then both omit it). A Loki bar chart can include the last bar past a range that ends before now and can miss up to one step at the range start. Quote the range stats; treat bars after a restart as estimates. Counted with counter_inc (see the folder README): hosted VMs are short-lived and each is its own series, which increase() and rate() would undercount. Counter totals can read high after a host changes instance id; Loki/Tempo are the reference.

panels.description: All log lines per bucket by slug. All six factory slugs are always listed; an idle slug shows 0. Each bar is the count of matching log lines in the bucket starting at it (bucket = $bucket): the point at t covers (t, t+step]. Loki uses $__auto with step=$bucket and a one-step negative offset so the in-progress bucket is included (a 5m bucket over more than about 38 days exceeds Loki's 11,000-point limit). On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. On a range that ends before now, the last bar covers its whole bucket and can include up to one step after the range end. LogQL has no subqueries, so a Loki bar cannot be capped at $__to. The first bar starts at the first step boundary at or after the range start, so events between the range start and that boundary (up to one step) are in the range stats but in no bar, and the left edge can show a gap. Quote the range stats.

list.description: Width of each bar in the per-bucket panels. Prometheus widens the step on long ranges; Loki stays on this value. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. Prometheus stops the last bar at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) and keeps the bar that straddles $__from. A range end off that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step out of both the bars and the range stats; the two still agree. On a range that ends before now, a Loki last bar covers its whole bucket and can include up to one step after the range end. The first Loki bar starts at the first step boundary at or after the range start, so the left edge can show a gap.
